source.title: Lesions of dorsolateral striatum preserve outcome expectancy but disrupt habit formation in instrumental learning

confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily replicated lesion dissociation from the Balleine lab. Provides the single cleanest instance of the 'dissociable lesion signature' Q-019 makes central to the three-gate hypothesis: excitotoxic lesion of the dorsolateral striatum abolishes habit formation (behaviour reverts to outcome-devaluation-sensitive goal-directed control) while lesion of the dorsomedial striatum leaves habit intact -- a double dissociation of two anatomically distinct striatal territories serving distinct control modes. Confidence held below 0.8 because the DMS/DLS axis is goal-directed-vs-habitual, which maps onto the sensorimotor/action-commitment leg of Q-019 (loop 3 and its automaticity gradient) but is not a 1:1 image of the full sensorium/thought/motor triad, and because rodent instrumental habit must transfer to the REE commit-gate construct.
failure_signatures: If commit-gating were implemented by a single convergent gate rather than separable territories, then removing the putative habit/sensorimotor territory should degrade action selection globally rather than selectively abolishing outcome-insensitive (habitual) responding while sparing goal-directed control -- the opposite of what the DLS lesion produces.

If the DLS territory were a generic motor-output stage rather than a distinct gating locus, DLS lesion should impair lever-pressing capability generally; instead it leaves responding intact but restores outcome sensitivity, indicating loss of a specific control mode, not a motor deficit.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The dorsolateral striatum is necessary for habit formation: DLS lesions render interval-trained instrumental responding sensitive to outcome devaluation again (goal-directed), whereas dorsomedial striatum lesions do not, establishing a DMS/DLS functional double dissociation in instrumental control.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the three-gate reading of Q-019's substrate question: commit-gating is served by anatomically separable gating territories with dissociable lesion signatures, not a single convergent gate. The DLS-as-habit result instantiates loop 3 (action-commitment / sensorimotor) and its automaticity gradient -- over-trained/automated behaviour migrates to a distinct sensorimotor territory whose removal selectively strips the automated mode while sparing the deliberate (goal-directed) mode.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The DMS/DLS dissociation is a two-territory goal-directed-vs-habit axis, not the three-way sensorium/thought/motor axis Q-019 posits; the paper evidences dissociability-in-principle and the action-commitment leg specifically, not the sensorium or thought gates. Rodent lever-press habit is a narrow behavioural proxy for the REE commit boundary.
mapping.source_context: Excitotoxic (quinolinic acid) lesions in Long-Evans rats; instrumental lever-pressing for sucrose under interval schedules; outcome devaluation by lithium-chloride-induced taste aversion; extinction test.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (canonical, replicated, causal lesion + devaluation design). Mapping_fidelity moderate-high because the dissociable-lesion signature is exactly the three-gate prediction, discounted because the axis is two-territory not three. Transfer_risk moderate: well-established construct but rat-to-REE-substrate extrapolation.
